findings.description: Critical: Due-deferral wake from `store --prune-only` is not durable across the rest of the same CYCLE when the tree also changes. `_maintenance` correctly flips due stubs to pending and `_lifecycle_rebuild` publishes that pending state, but `SKILL.md` keeps using the pre-maintenance `$SUPERVISE_RECORD` for later `prepare-batch` and `rank`. Those commands re-read the stale deferred+until entry, put the stub back in the future-deferred bucket, and overwrite the mirror with deferred again. Independently reproduced: after wake the mirror is pending; after prepare-batch+rank with the stale record it is deferred/`2026-09-15` again.
findings.resolution: After successful non-dry-run prune-only, reload the supervisor record from the updated mirror (or have store return the maintained decisions) before prepare-batch/rank; also make prepare-batch/rank apply the same due-wake rule from as_of so a stale host record cannot re-defer already-due work.

findings.description: Critical: `prepare_batch` trusts host-supplied decision state and never applies due-wake itself (lines 845-868), while `rank_candidates` copies `decision`/`until` from that same prior index into the published digest and mirror (lines 618-628 and 703-716). This is the code-side half of finding 1: even with a corrected SKILL reload, any caller that passes a pre-maintenance record can silently undo lifecycle wake on a scored cycle.
findings.resolution: Share one decision-normalization helper used by store maintenance, prepare-batch, and rank so due deferred entries become pending before ranking/publication, regardless of which record snapshot the host threaded in.

findings.description: Nit: After a terminal reject/approve is pruned, `store_candidates` will re-admit the same stub_key as fresh and count it toward the 20-candidate cap, but `prepare_batch` unconditionally skips approved/rejected decisions and therefore omits that file from the manifest. Independently reproduced: re-admitted rejected key is stored and listed in `fresh_keys`, yet `prepare_batch` returns `requested_keys: []`, so the slot is consumed by invisible work until the next prune-only pass.
findings.resolution: On fresh admission of a key with a terminal durable decision, either refuse with an explicit error, or supersede that terminal history to pending for the new payload; do not leave store files that prepare-batch will always ignore.

findings.description: FYI: `test_prepare_batch_output_is_deterministic_and_at_most_64_kib` asserts length using compact `separators=(',', ':')` JSON without the trailing newline, while production `_manifest_bytes` / CLI stdout use default-spaced `json.dumps(...)+'\n'`. The production bound itself is correct and covered by the stdout-serialization rejection test; this assertion would not catch a regression that only overflows the real encoding.
findings.resolution: Align the assertion with `_manifest_bytes` / exact stdout encoding, or assert via the same helper the runtime uses.

findings.description: none: Journal recovery now fail-closes correctly: `_authorize_transaction_target` allowlists only candidate/cache/digest/mirror paths with operation-appropriate verbs, and `recover_transaction` validates schema version, bounds, duplicates, and checksums for every operation before mutating any target. Tampered-target and oversized-journal tests pin the bypass that impl-findings #1 closed.

none: The rubric trust boundary matches the hardened contract: `prepare_batch` embeds `ready_set` inside the single manifest, measures exact stdout serialization via `_manifest_bytes`, enforces the 64 KiB cap (including individually oversized stubs), frames provenance as untrusted data after `sanitize_string`, and the prompt places trusted instructions before the untrusted manifest block.

none: Terminal lifecycle history is handled cleanly at the module boundary: active pending/deferred entries are ranked from the live backlog, while `_merge_terminal_history` preserves approved/rejected decisions in the durable mirror without keeping those keys in the active store or ranked digest. That matches design D5 and closes impl-findings #4 without conflating payload files and supervisor facts.

none: Provenance loading is bounded the way impl-findings #9 required: `_artifact_evidence` opens a binary handle and reads only `MAX_EVIDENCE_BYTES + 1`, with a regression test that fails if the full artifact is slurped via `Path.read_bytes`.

none: Publication resilience is solid for the scored and lifecycle paths: operations are staged in a fsynced roll-forward journal, non-digest targets are applied first, `digest.json` is replaced last, checksums make recovery idempotent, and read-only/dry-run entry points refuse mixed state while mutating commands recover first.

none: Compatibility with the existing supervisor record surface is preserved: canonical and mirror schemas gain optional decision metadata with conditional requirements, `cycle_state._clean_digested_stub` round-trips those fields, fingerprint exclusions keep store/cache/digest/journal commits from self-invalidating the cycle, and the `.agents`/`.claude` supervise mirrors are byte-identical to the canonical skill.
